label: WILL_CAPACITY_VERSUS_WILLED_GIVING_2: a rational power gives x, not at a same-set-up world
definition: WilledTwoWayAt F A w y: as PropensityChanceAt F A w y with the power rational: y exists at w, and there are a rational power p of y, a being x and a world v accessible from w where y exists with the same set-up, such that y gives x being at w by p and does not give x being at v.
note: Analyst definition, attribution deferred (docs/notes/will-versus-chance.md). Example: on Aquinas's account, God giving a creature being by his will, which 'determinat seipsam' to an object to which it has a non-necessary relation (ST I q.19 a.3 ad 5, navigation). It differs from CHANCE_3 only in Rational (flip law). It does not say that the exercise is explained contrastively; the luck objection to undetermined choice is not answered by the definition. Implies TwoWayGiverAt (DEF e006ddeb).
